sources.name: OGC GeoTIFF Standard 1.1
sources.role: Raster-to-model georeference and CRS metadata contract
verified_facts: GeoTIFF 1.1 defines TIFF tags and GeoKeys for georeferenced or geocoded raster imagery.
Raster-to-model positioning uses ModelTiepointTag with ModelPixelScaleTag, or ModelTransformationTag.
GeoTIFF includes model CRS requirements, including projected and vertical CRS keys.
semantic_limits: Valid GeoTIFF metadata does not prove the numeric accuracy or freshness of elevation samples.
Horizontal georeference alone does not prove that heights use ODN or any required vertical CRS.
RasterPixelIsArea versus RasterPixelIsPoint semantics must not be silently interchanged.

sources.name: OGC Cloud Optimized GeoTIFF Standard 1.0
sources.role: Full-resolution IFD, overview and byte-range delivery contract
verified_facts: COG organizes TIFF or BigTIFF data using tiles, optional reduced-resolution subfiles and GeoTIFF keys.
Reduced-resolution subfiles are downsampled images with less detail than the full-resolution image.
Full-resolution IFDs carry the georeference; HTTP range permits retrieval of only needed byte fragments.
semantic_limits: An overview is not accepted for parcel-height measurement when full-resolution cells are required.
COG conformance and fast byte-range access do not establish elevation accuracy.
A successful partial byte request does not prove that the complete raster or all required tiles were read.

sources.name: OGC CoverageJSON Community Standard 1.0
sources.role: Coverage domain, referencing, axis-order and missing-value contract
verified_facts: CoverageJSON separates coverage domain, parameters and ranges.
Domain axes and spatial referencing must be declared, and range shape/axis names must correspond to the domain.
Null values in NdArray ranges represent missing data.
semantic_limits: Null range values are excluded rather than interpreted as zero elevation.
Schema conformance does not prove authoritative source identity, vertical datum or measurement accuracy.
Row-major array order and axis names must be resolved before sampling.

sources.name: RFC 9110 HTTP Semantics — Range Requests
verified_facts: A 206 response transfers one or more parts of a selected representation.
Content-Range identifies the enclosed range and can state the complete representation length.
Multiple partial responses can be safely combined only under the response rules, including a common strong validator.
semantic_limits: HTTP 206 success is not treated as complete-object readback.
Content-Length on a 206 response normally describes the message part, not the complete representation.
Partial ranges cannot be promoted to a complete raster without coverage accounting and integrity validation.
